answer: Arrival-time prism gating. Each new identity must submit its first N actions through a spread of arrival delays, and the agent scores the timing profile against a target shape; clones released in bursts cluster at the nadir of the delay distribution and get throttled. The rule: burst-arrival accounts are queued behind shaped-traffic accounts, so a sybil swarm gains near-zero early throughput. The comet test—whether an identity's traffic grows smoothly or spikes—decides promotion.
